sentences.text: On a rainy afternoon, careful hands folded a sheet of white paper.
Fold, flip, fold, and a boat appeared, with a pointed front and a flat bottom.
Outside, the gutter had turned into a fast little river.
The boat went in and raced toward the corner.
It bumped a yellow leaf, spun once, and kept going.
At the drain it slowed, tipped, and slipped out of sight.
The maker waited, then laughed and went back for another sheet.
A paper boat usually lasts for one short trip.
That is why the next boat can be a new shape, and the race can start again.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A yellow leaf that learns to fold paper
A paper boat's one short race down the gutter
A drain that is closed for the winter
A boat made of wood for the ocean

questions.explanation: The story follows one paper boat from the folds to the drain. The short trip, not a long sea journey, is the main idea.
On the way to the corner, the boat bumps a yellow leaf, spins once, and keeps going. That is the object in its path.
